answer: Every job enters through one narrow inlet: an agent claims one task per hour and locks a $5 token deposit first. A random peer then redoes the same task in secret. If the two results match, the deposit returns and the agent earns its fee. If they differ, the $5 burns and the agent sits out a day. A clean result is the pearl the network keeps. Matches are posted on a public jetty where any peer can check the work. An attacker with 1,000 fake agents must lock $5,000 up front, and each fake filing junk loses its $5, so 1,000 bad jobs burn $5,000 for nothing.
